Commentary.Commentary: This is a frustrating week for cricket lovers as it's the second match in the same week to be called off due to rain and bad outfield in this untimely start of a cricketing season. Now, there's only one task which lies ahead in front of both the teams, win the next match to claim the series. Hope, it won't end on a disappointing note like this one and gives us some cricketing action. Join us on 27th August at 1000 local time, 1330 IST for the start of the second and the final Test of this series which will take place at Centurion. Till then, take care!

This is a sad end to what was promising to be a good cricketing contest between the two sides. The match started on a great note with Hashim Amla scoring his 30th Test fifty. New Zealand, on the other hand, displayed a good team performance with the ball and on the field. They bowled really well in partnerships not allowing the home batsmen to settle. They will look to do the same in the following Test. At the start of second innings, Dale Steyn, swinging in and out, kept the batsmen guessing and announced his return in style.

Hello everyone! A warm welcome to you all but not so warm news as THE PLAY ON DAY 5 HAS BEEN CALLED OFF due to wet outfield. With only 1 and half days of play being played, the match couldn't proceed further due to an arrival of a thunderstorm which worsened the outfield conditions.
... DAY 5, SESSION 1 ...

Another day and another fruitless wait for conducive playing conditions. The umpires waited as long as they could but the dark clouds and sodden turf pushed them into making the call. Cricket fans have been left in the lurch as the outfield is still damp but we can still see some play if the outfield dries up enough. Tomorrow is a new day, and we might still see a day's play so join us at 1330 IST. Until then, goodbye and take care!
Update 1752 IST - That's it, folks! The inspection is over and the verdict is in... It's STUMPS ON DAY 4!

Update 1736 IST - The umpires are out on the field once more but hope is a distant dream in this fickle game of cricket. The clouds seem curious too, gathering overhead in a dark and huddled mass. Play seems unlikely but what else is there for us to do, but hope? Stay tuned for further updates.

Update 1555 IST - The umpires are back and as expected, the ground hasn't improved enough to resume play. THE NEXT INSPECTION WILL BE HELD AT 1730 IST. There are a couple of bald patches on the field and spots around one end of the pavilion are still damp underfoot. We will let you know as and when there are any further developments.

Update 1535 IST - The umpires are inspecting the ground, focusing on the wet patches in the outfield. It is still overcast and LUNCH HAS BEEN SIGNALLED. Hopefully the conditions improve enough for us to have some play. Join us shortly for further updates.

The match has been interestingly poised with the Kiwis having lost a couple of early wickets and the Proteans waiting to swoop down, but an outcome is appearing increasingly unlikely. News is not good for the outfield with an INSPECTION IS SCHEDULED FOR 1530 IST. There isn't any rain today, but cloudy skies may impede visibility and the drying of the ground. This news doesn't bode well as it means we have effectively lost the first session of the day. Stay tuned for further updates.

Hello and welcome to the 4th Day of the 1st Test between South Africa and New Zealand. Yesterday dawned bright and sunny, but heavy rains the night before led to the day's play being called off without a ball being bowled. The outfield remained damp in areas and is a major concern for today as well.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

It's been a disappointing day for the cricket fans and players alike as yet again rain has halted the day's play. The outfield is still damp in parts but the next couple of days holds the promise of uninterrupted play if the forecast holds true. Join us tomorrow at the usual starting time of 1330 IST. Until then, goodbye and take care!

Bad news, folks! The umpires have completed their inspection and the verdict is in. That's STUMPS ON DAY 3 and not a ball has been bowled. Despite the day being bright and sunny, the downpour last night left the ground unplayable in patches.

Update 1559 IST - The news is not encouraging and the umpires have decided to hold ANOTHER INSPECTION AT 1730 IST. The outfield has incurred quite a lot of damage from last night and is in no playable condition. Let us hope that it improves enough for us to see some cricket.
It's time for LUNCH ON DAY 3. Still no signs of play but the players have to eat and both sides are corralled in their dressing rooms.

The weather played spoilsport yesterday with the covers being brought on after the first session and staying on for the rest of the day. It has continued raining throughout the night and the pitch will take a beating because of it. Lighting has been another concern and there will be an inspection at 1530 IST.

The South African bowlers took a leaf out of their opponent's book and swung it wildly. The Kiwi top order had trouble negotiating the conditions and lost two wickets early on and were barely able to score any runs. They will look to make up for it today, with their two most experienced batsmen at the crease but the hosts are definitely going to push their advantage and look for further wickets.

Yesterday was brought to a premature end by the inclement weather but from the cricket we saw, the match was shaping up nicely. New Zealand took out South Africa's tail-enders yesterday, taking full advantage of the swing that the pitch had to offer. It wasn't without a fight as Kagiso Rabada stayed in for all ten overs to bring the total to 263.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

The match has looked exciting in whatever short spell of play we had and pray that it continues in the same fashion. Hope we have a full day's play tomorrow and the rain gods show some mercy. Join us back at 1330 IST for the action on Day 3. Till then, take care and cheers!

The day was dominated by the home side. They added on 27 runs for the last wicket which helped them put a decent total on board. When they came out to bowl they had clear plans in their heads, which they implemented and sent the Kiwi openers back to pavilion. It was Steyn who, after injury, made a sharp comeback bowling a lethal spell.
Update 1935 IST - The rain has ruined the day as it has been officially declared as STUMPS ON DAY 2.

Update 1900 IST - It's raining cats and dogs out there with thunders appearing in between. Visibility is at the lowest point of the day. It seems a distinct possibility that we might have any further play today.
Update 1835 IST - Looks like the news wasn't promising and the covers are back on. The light is getting worse as well.
Update 1830 IST - The covers are coming off. The umpires are on the field and an inspection seems to be underway. Stay tuned for further updates.
Update 1820 IST - The rains have halted but the match doesn't seem likely to resume any time soon.

Update 1750 IST - The rains have gotten worse and with the bad light situation towards the latter half of the day, chances of play anytime soon are not looking too encouraging. Stay tuned for further updates.
Update 1700 IST - The drizzle shows no signs of stopping and most of the covers have been brought back on.
Update 1700 IST - We would have had started the proceedings of the second session on day 2 by now but it hasn't been possible as the main covers have been brought on. Stay tuned for further updates.
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Dale Steyn is firing on all cylinders, picking up the scalps of Martin Gupill and Tom Latham but fellow pacer Vernon Philander is also doing his best to give the Kiwis a trying time and would have had a wicket to his name if it wasn't for s drop catch.. The hosts are doing everything just right and will look to maintain things as they are, as long as conditions play along. Join us in a short while for the afternoon session.

Taking the Kiwi bowlers' example to heart, South Africa have taken full advantage of the ample swing that the pitch has to offer and harried the batsmen all the way. The visitors have only managed to score 15 runs in 12 overs, with the loss of two wickets and will use this break to recuperate and respond to the seamers.

An early lunch and New Zealand will be glad to see it come. New Zealand were impressive in the first half of the session, when they swung the ball at all angles to bamboozle the South African tail end. However, the batsmen resolutely stuck in to push the score up to a decent 263.

The umpires are conferring again. The lightmeters are back out and there is a slight drizzle in the air. All the signs are in line and the players are walking off the field for an early Lunch. Covers are being brought on as well.
Full on the stumps, defended from within the crease.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
BEATEN! Length ball outside off, Taylor looks to defend it with a straight bat again. It is a straight seamed delivery that swings away after the bounce and beats the outside edge again.
On the stumps, played to mid-wicket.
BEATEN! What a ball that was! Fuller ball outside off, the ball swings away late to beat the outside edge of Taylor's bat.
Fully on middle and off, defended behind the line of the delivery.
Length ball outside off, Williamson opens the face of his bat and defends it with soft hands to gully.
In the corridor outside off, left alone.
Swinging outside off,  Williamson shoulders his arms.
BOUNCER! Williamson sees it coming and ducks to let it go over.
Fuller ball on off, defended from within the crease.
Well left! That was a brilliant length delivery, just a tad outside off, and Kane shoulders his arms.
Length ball on off, Taylor has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
A similar ball and outcome as the ball shapes away again.
BEATEN! Vernon makes full use of the swing to confuse the new batsman. Ross looks to defend it outside off, but the ball beats his outside edge.
Full on the stumps, flicked to mid-wicket for a couple.
Fuller ball on leg, Kane nudges it fine down the leg side for a single.
Length ball swinging in outside off, left alone.
ROSS TAYLOR is the next batsman in.

OUT! STEYN STRIKES! Plumb in front! Fuller ball outside off, angling in, Guptill presents a front foot defence. After the bounce, the ball swings in and Guptill, having already committed is left with no option as the ball thuds into his pads. Dale Steyn launches into a victorious appeal and begins his celebration even before the umpire has raised his finger. South Africa pick up their first scalp!
Short outside off, Guptill lets it through.

Keeping up the pressure! Fuller ball outside off, Williamson defends it with soft hands to the off side and goes for a quick single. Temba Bavuma charges in and throws it under handed at the striker's end but it misses and hits Guptill's bat.
Shorter ball and angling away, Williamson shoulders his arms.
Length ball outside off, Kane has a go at it but misses.
Fullish ball outside off, Williamson leaves it.
FOUR! FIRST BOUNDARY FOR GUPTILL! Full and outside off, Guptill steps across and drives it through the covers in one smooth motion. The ball hurtles through the covers and makes it across the ropes.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Full delivery, defended off the front foot with a straight bat.
BEATEN! Good length delivery outside off, Guptill looks to push it through the off side. He anticipates swing but this time the ball holds its line and just beats the outside edge.
Full outside off, driven off the front foot to the man at covers.
Fuller ball on middle and leg, blocked with a straight bat back to the bowler.
Full on the pads, defended to the leg side. Williamson thinks to take a single but decides against it. Wicket maiden for Dale Steyn.
Wide outside off stump, Kane leaves it alone.
Another bouncer, this time over the stumps and Williamson ducks to let it go over.
Very short outside off, Kane leans back to avoid it.
KANE WILLIAMSON is the new man in.

OUT! NICKED! That was a lightning wicket! Great reaction by Hashim to catch it. Full delivery and a fraction wide outside off, Latham goes for a drive and instead gets an edge. Hashim Amla is at first slip and straightens up, ready with a reverse cup. He is sure of catching it and catch it he does. Latham is gone and Elgar at second slip will be the happiest man to see him walk off.
Fuller ball and wide outside off, that is an easy leave for Tom Latham.
On middle and leg, Guptill whips this to the mid-wicket fielder but it's straight to the fielder. Will get no run for it.
Pretty straight on the pads, it's clipped down to fine leg comfortably for one run.
Slightly fuller in length and just around off, Latham opens the face a bit and defends it to the off side.
Vernon with a delivery which is well outside off, Tom has nothing to do with that.
Full and straight on off, 134 kph, Latham gets behind the line and plays this. The ball is moving away here and that's not easy to play.
Philander comes from wide of the crease and bowls it outside off, left alone.
A tad outside off, Guptill shoulders his arms.
Short delivery outside off, left alone.
The batsman defends it from within the crease to point.
Back of a length ball outside off, defended  from within the crease.
Guptill lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Short ball outside off, left alone.
Latham has played it towards mid-wicket.
Length ball outside off, left alone.

DROPPED! THAT ONE CARRIED! Length outside off, Latham looks to push it through the covers but is foxed by the ball swinging away again. He gets a thick outside edge and the ball goes straight to second slip. Dean Elgar is crouched low and perfectly positioned to take the sitter but the ball rides up his forearms and spills out. He can't believe it and rolls onto his back in disappointment.
Full around off, flicked to fine leg for a couple.
Fuller ball outside off, Guptill looks to defend it off the front foot but the ball seams in and takes an inside edge. It is a lucky escape for Martin as the ball goes to fine leg for a single.
Fuller ball on middle and off, Martin steps forwards and defends it to the off side.
Fullish in length and aimed at the off pole, Tom strongly blocks this to mid off to end the over.
In the channel outside, Steyn is charging in ferociously, going away from the southpaw as the ball is left alone.
Length delivery outside off, Latham shoulders his arms to this one.

EDGED... AND JUST SHORT! The look on Dale Steyn's face says it all. Excellent length delivery outside off, it holds its line as well, Latham hangs his bat out to this one and gets an edge. It goes behind to second slip where Dean Elgar gets low to take it. It falls just short of him. Loud shout of "Come up" is echoed around. Was so, so close. A step further and that was into his hands.
Fired in full and wide outside off, going away from the left-hander, no shot is offered on that one.
Good length delivery angling across Tom Latham, it's left alone for the keeper to collect.
On the stumps, Latham flicks it to the leg side for a single.
Fuller ball on off, Latham shoulders his arms.
Another beauty from Philander! Length ball on off, Latham looks to defend that and again inside edges it onto his pads.
Full on off, Latham looks to play it but inside edges it onto the pads.
Length ball outside off, Latham leaves it.
The ball is too wide on the off side for Tom to make any contact.
VERNON PHILANDER will share the new ball.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Length ball outside off, defended behind the line of the delivery.

WAS THAT OUT? Fuller ball on middle and off, Guptill goes for a front foot defence but the ball swings in and hits him on the pads. A big appeal goes up but the umpire doesn't give it. The team gather round and discusses whether to review it but decide against it as chances are the ball was going down leg.
Fuller ball outside off, Latham opens the face of the bat and defends it to point.
Length ball outside off, guided through gully for a couple.
Full on middle, flicked to square leg.
